newsitem.title: UK: Manchester Utd first half profit rises.
newsitem.headline: Manchester Utd first half profit rises.

text.p: English soccer champions Manchester United Plc said on Monday pre-tax profit for the first six months of its financial year rose to 19.45 million pounds ($31.78 million) from 15.28 million pounds.

Improved television revenues, higher home crowds and strong growth in merchandising lifted turnover by 68 percent to 50.1 million pounds in the six months to end-January. Profits were also boosted by net transfer income of 3.8 million pounds.
United, European Cup semi-finalists and English league leaders, lifted its interim dividend to 1.9 pence per share from 1.6 pence, an increase of almost 19 percent.

"Investment continues in the Old Trafford stadium to improve facilities for our supporters: further investment in the merchandising division is also taking place," chairman Professor Sir Roland Smith said in a statement.
"Your board continues to apply its energies to ensuring that Manchester United participates in all the exciting changes taking shape in the sports and television industries," he added.

United's crowds have increased following the completion of building work at Old Trafford which had restricted attendances in 1996. Television revenue has been lifted by the new premier league deal with BSkyB and the club's success in Europe. ($1=.6120 Pound)
